record.paper_title: Realistic shell-model calculations: current status and open problems
record.original_question: Why is the agreement between theory and experiment generally worse for nuclei in which hole-hole interaction matrix elements are relevant than for nuclei dominated by particle-particle or particle-hole matrix elements, and what physical or methodological origin explains this asymmetry?

evidence.quote: While the overall agreement between theory and experiment may be considered satisfactory in most cases, it is not in general of the same quality as that obtained for nuclei in which there is no hole-hole interaction.
At present, we don’t have a clear understanding of the origin of this dissimetry.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the realistic nuclear shell-model framework, one starts from a realistic nucleon-nucleon potential (e.g., derived from meson-exchange or chiral effective field theory) and constructs, via many-body perturbation theory (such as the folded-diagram or Q-box expansion), an effective two-body interaction acting in a chosen valence model space outside a doubly closed-shell core. The two-body matrix elements of this effective interaction can be classified, according to whether the valence nucleons are treated as particles above the core or as holes in a closed shell, into three types: particle-particle (pp), particle-hole (ph), and hole-hole (hh) matrix elements.

When such effective interactions are used to compute spectra, binding energies, and electromagnetic observables, empirical observation across a range of nuclei indicates that the agreement between the calculated quantities and experimental data is systematically worse for nuclei whose low-lying structure is dominated by hole-hole matrix elements than for nuclei dominated by particle-particle or particle-hole matrix elements.

Problem. Identify and justify the physical and/or methodological origin of this asymmetry. Specifically:
(a) Determine which features of the perturbative construction of the effective interaction (choice of unperturbed single-particle/single-hole energies, treatment of intermediate-state Pauli blocking, convergence of the Q-box and folded-diagram series, truncation of the model space, or omission of three-nucleon forces) are responsible for the systematically reduced quality of hh matrix elements relative to pp and ph matrix elements.
(b) Provide a quantitative or qualitative argument explaining why the same procedure that reproduces pp- and ph-dominated spectra well degrades when applied to hh-dominated nuclei.
artifact.status_search_result: The original source explicitly states that there is no clear understanding of the origin of this asymmetry. Subsequent reviews on realistic shell-model calculations (e.g., Coraggio, Covello, Gargano, Itaco, Kuo) continue to discuss limitations of effective interactions including missing three-nucleon forces and Pauli-blocking effects but do not present a definitive explanation specific to the hh-vs-pp/ph asymmetry. The question therefore appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Realistic shell-model calculations: current status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: At present, we don't have a clear understanding of the origin of this dissimetry.
status_evidence.claim: The asymmetry in agreement quality between hh-dominated nuclei and pp/ph-dominated nuclei is not understood.
